memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not take interest or any profit from them, but fear your God, so that
they may continue to live among you. You must not lend them money at
interest or sell them food at a profit'" - Lev 25:36-37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God forbids charging interest to a fellow Israelite who has fallen into
poverty. To profit from a desperate neighbour's need was off limits. And
again the reason is given: fear your God.

We must understand the setting. This was not a ban on all lending or
banking. It was a specific protection for the poor among God's covenant
people. To pile interest onto someone already drowning in need was to
profit from their misery — and God would not allow His people to treat one
another that way.

Dear friend, the underlying principle is timeless: the vulnerability of
others is not an opportunity for our gain. Wherever someone is desperate,
the temptation exists to exploit that desperation for profit. God calls His
people to the opposite instinct — to relieve the desperate, not to squeeze
them.

The psalmist describes the person who may dwell with God as one who lends
money to the poor without interest (Ps 15:5). Jesus went further, telling
His followers to lend without expecting anything back, because that
reflects the mercy of the Most High (Luke 6:34-36).

This cuts against every instinct that says get the maximum return. God asks:
when your neighbour is down, will you profit from them or lift them up?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever been tempted to profit from someone's desperation?
2. How can I lift up the vulnerable rather than exploit their need?
3. Does my generosity reflect the mercy God has shown me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, keep me from ever profiting from another person's desperation. Give
me a heart that lifts up the struggling, reflecting Your mercy to me. Amen.
